title: Patagonia island tree: multi-shot exposure blending, edge refinement, and selective color editing (documented workflow)

locations.name: Patagonia region (probable)
locations.basis: Filename path includes 'Patagonia'; transcript references 'Fitzroy' (a notable Patagonia location) and 'Iceland' as folder labels; no explicit confirmation of shooting location

summary: This video documents a landscape editing workflow centered on a sunlit island tree, with the presenter comparing a better-lit frame to an earlier take and then executing a two-exposure composite: a dark sky and bright foreground. The process includes selecting the exposures, blending them, painting the original tree back into the composite, and refining the edge with brushes. The workflow also covers isolating the tree with selective color adjustments, applying dehaze and warmth for mood, and using targeted color grading to separate foreground and background. Throughout, the speaker emphasizes careful edge work, opacity control, and minimal processing to preserve a natural look, while discussing composition and crop rules (rule of thirds) and noting equipment and file organization cues.
topics: Subject framing and rule of thirds
Layer masking and brush-based edge refinement
Hard vs soft brush edge control

sections.title: Two-exposure planning for sky and foreground
sections.description: The speaker identifies the sky as overexposed in some frames and discusses using separate exposures (sky vs. foreground) to control different areas, including references to AEB/bracketing approaches.

sections.title: Initial blending approach and radiant light
concepts: Paint-in of sky and mountain tops
Radiant light emanating from the sun location
sections.description: Demonstrates painting in the sky and top of the mountain from the sky-exposure layer to achieve a radiant light effect on the island, creating the sense of sunlit atmosphere in the composite.

sections.title: Edge refinement and tree reintroduction
sections.description: Explains careful reintroduction of the original tree on the island by painting with high-precision brushes, refining the edge, using fades to blend, and ensuring seamless transitions at 80–90% opacity before final refinements.

sections.title: Selective color and local color isolation
concepts: Isolating blacks to darken tree tops
sections.description: Describes using selective color to isolate the tree top from the background, then applying targeted darkening to the tree while preserving the surrounding water and sky; discusses maintaining harmony with color balance.

sections.title: Telephoto notes and final processing remarks
sections.description: Notes about telephoto shots from earlier in the sequence, with a reminder to avoid over-processing and to favor natural-looking adjustments; closes with reflections on various shots and processing limits.
